prompt: I am fact-checking an encyclopedia entry on psilocybin against this European Union Drugs Agency (EUDA, formerly EMCDDA) page or document. Rules: report only what this page itself prints, exactly as printed (same spelling, capitalization, punctuation, hyphens, primes, Greek letters, brackets). Give every number digit by digit as printed. Give every list complete, every entry, in page order, none skipped or merged. Do not add anything from outside the page. Write 'not on page' for any item the page does not have. Copy wording only as short phrases of at most 15 words. Do not include dosage amounts or instructions for use. answer:
**Fact-check extraction: EUDA "Hallucinogenic mushrooms drug profile"**

**(1) Names and identifiers**

- **Psilocybin:** "Psilocybin (PY, 4-phosphoryloxy-N,N-dimethyltryptamine)" (first Chemistry paragraph; the second paragraph prints "NN-dimethyltryptamine"). Other names: "psilocybine, psilocibina, psilocybinum, psylosybiini". CAS-number: 520-52-5. IUPAC: "[3-(2-dimethylaminoethyl)-1H-indol-4-yl] dihydrogen phosphate". Molecular formula: C12H17N204P. Molecular weight: 284.3 g/mol.
- **Psilocin:** "psilocine, psilocyn". CAS-number 520-53-6. Also "4-hydroxy-NN-dimethyltryptamine (4-OH-DMT)" and "3-(2-dimethylaminoethyl)indol-4-ol". IUPAC: "3-(2-dimethylaminoethyl)-1H-indol-4-ol". Molecular formula: C12H16N20. Molecular weight: 204.3 g/mol.
- **Other abbreviations on the page:** 5-HT, 5-hydroxytryptamine, 5-HT1A, 5-HT2A, 5-HT2C, DMT.
- **ATC codes:** not on page.
- **Drug codes/schedules:** "Schedule I of the United Nations 1971 Convention on Psychotropic Substances".

**(2) Forms, preparations, products and related compounds**

- "available in fresh form"; "treated/preserved (e.g. deliberately dried, cooked, frozen)"; "dry powders or capsules".
- "small brown or tan mushrooms" (appearance); flesh of *Psilocybe* "turns blue or green when bruised or cut".
- *Psilocybe cubensis* varieties (cultivated, mostly in the Netherlands); *Psilocybe tampensis* (named in growkit definition).
- Genera: *Psilocybe*, *Panaeolus*, *Copelandia*; "number exceeds 50 species".
- Products named: "spore prints", "spawnbags", "growkits", "by-products" [sales context omitted by reader 2].
- Synthetic form: "can be produced synthetically, but this form of the drug is not often found".
- Brand name: "Indocybin®" (pure synthetic psilocybin, marketed by Sandoz in the 1960s).
- Related compounds: baeocystin, norbaeocystin, bufotenine, LSD, mescaline, MDMA, DMT, ibogaine, ketamine, serotonin, tryptophan, muscimol, ibotenic acid.
- Lookalike species: *Agaricus bisporus*; *Amanita muscaria* (fly agaric).

**(3) Street, slang and common names (page order)**

Listed as "Common names in the English language are": shrooms; magic mushrooms; sacred mushrooms; teonanácatl.

Listed as "Various terms have also been used by users" (attributed to "Martindale, 2007"; no country, region or date given): blue caps; boomers; booms; buttons; caps; champ; fungus; funguys; God's flesh; hombrecitos; las mujercitas; little smoke; Mexican mushroom; mushies; mushroom soup; mushroom tea; mushrooms; musk; pizza toppings; rooms; silly putty; simple Simun; zoomers.

A separate translations list gives terms for "hallucinogenic mushrooms", not slang: magické houby; psilocybinsvampe; magiske svampe; hallutsinogeense toimega seened; μαγικά μανιτάρια; champignons hallucinogènes; champis; Psychoaktive Pilze; Zauberpilze; varázsgombák; hallucinogén gombák; pszilocibingombák; funghi magici; Halucinogēnās (maģiskās) sēnes; haliucinogeniniai grybai; magiškieji grybai; fleinsopp; magiczne grzybki; grzyby halucynogenne; cogumelos mágicos; cogumelos psicadélicos; magické huby; čudeţne gobe; hongos alucinógenos; hongos lisérgicos; honguitos; ciuperci halucinogene; magiska svampar; psykedeliska svampar. (Bulgarian "магически гъби" and Estonian/Lithuanian/Slovenian entries are as printed.)

**(4) Title and dates**

- Page title (metadata): "Hallucinogenic mushrooms drug profile | The European Union Drugs Agency (EUDA)".
- Heading: "Hallucinogenic mushrooms drug profile".
- Publication or last-updated date for this profile: not on page. Dates shown (June 2026, June 2025, etc.) belong to other "Publications" items.

**Completeness note:** The page content appears complete for this profile. The only apparent gaps are the "Show more" link and the PDF-preparation notice, which are navigation text rather than profile content.
